One internal repository, 7 future test tasks, 24 learning commits. Configurations: skill-conditioned agent vs baseline agent without skills, under 4 conditions (sequential/parallel x by-category/all). Baseline: same agent and tools without skill document. Held constant: model (Claude Opus 4.6), tool-use capabilities, tasks. Acceptance: oracle diffs (no tests). Repetitions: not stated (apparently one run per condition). Human intervention: none stated

Skills better in 3 of 4 conditions: File IoU +19 pts in seq-all (80% vs 61%), +8 to +12 in par conditions, tie in seq-bycat; seq-all 21% fewer steps (56.8 vs 71.9); line deviation lower in 3 of 4. Win rates >50% in 3 of 4 settings per judge (seq-bycat 26%/46%, par-all 46% under Claude judge). Gains in Q2 logic (50% vs 25%) and Q3 redundancy; baseline slightly better on Q1 scope and Q4 style. No significance test

Partly distinguished conditions (seq-bycat no gain). Repeatability not assessed (7 tasks; baseline values differ between conditions although the baseline has no skills, not explained). Limitations stated: LLM-judge bias, single internal repository

Validated on one internal repository only; generalisation to open-source GitHub repositories needed; LLM judges may be biased or inaccurate, more verifiable metrics needed; transfer of skills to broader tasks and established benchmarks open; skills help localisation and reuse but not surface style; skills can induce over-caution (redundant guard)
